evaluations.evidence: search and discover music using content identification or fingerprinting
evaluations.rationale: “Content identification” vs “fingerprinting” and what inputs/sources are supported can be interpreted in materially different ways (audio snippet, full track, humming, etc.).

evaluations.evidence: based on my profile
evaluations.rationale: “My profile” is underspecified (which attributes, explicit vs implicit behavior), allowing different implementations.

evaluations.evidence: based on other users similar to myself
evaluations.rationale: “Similar” is ambiguous (similar taste, demographics, behavior, location, etc.), leading to materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: music or ringback tones similar to a given music video based on content similarity
evaluations.rationale: “Similar”/“content similarity” is unclear (audio similarity, visual similarity, metadata similarity), yielding different requirements.

evaluations.evidence: exploiting enriched metadata and image tags ... related artists, new genre, or other relevant listening path
evaluations.rationale: “Enriched metadata,” “image tags,” and “relevant listening path” are vague abstractions with multiple interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: upload tagged videos and have tags available for all further processing steps
evaluations.rationale: “Tags” (format, schema, source) and “all further processing steps” are unclear, allowing different scopes/behaviors.

evaluations.evidence: view thumbnail sequences of video segments
evaluations.rationale: “Thumbnail sequences” and what constitutes a “video segment” (fixed length, shot boundaries, admin-defined) are ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: get info about similar video items and segments
evaluations.rationale: “Info” and “similar” are underspecified; similarity basis and information content can vary materially.

evaluations.evidence: info about perceptually similar video items and segments
evaluations.rationale: “Perceptually similar” is ambiguous (visual only, audio-visual, human-perceived vs algorithmic), leading to different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: content recommendations from similar profiles
evaluations.rationale: “Content” and “similar profiles” are vague; profile definition and similarity criteria are unclear.

evaluations.evidence: based on most relevant news events in my area
evaluations.rationale: “Most relevant,” “news events,” and “my area” are ambiguous (radius, administrative region, personalization), enabling different requirements.

evaluations.evidence: identify persons in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: “Identify” (recognize specific individuals vs detect humans) and “related information” are materially ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: identify products in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: “Identify products” (detect category vs specific SKU/brand) and “related information” are unclear.

evaluations.evidence: identify broadcaster logos in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: “Identify” could mean detect presence vs determine which broadcaster; “related information” is unspecified.

evaluations.evidence: identify brands in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: “Identify brands” (logo detection, text recognition, product association) and “related information” are ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: recommended with videos related to that picture or image
evaluations.rationale: “Related” is ambiguous (visual similarity, same object, same location, same topic), leading to different recommendation behavior.

evaluations.evidence: access content using a geographical map ... videos covering the area, monuments or any other relevant point of interest
evaluations.rationale: “Covering the area” and “relevant point of interest” are vague; map interaction and coverage criteria can differ materially.

evaluations.evidence: search content items using automatic speech recognition
evaluations.rationale: “Content items” and how ASR is used for search (live query vs indexing, languages, fields searched) are underspecified.

evaluations.evidence: see, validate and edit segmentation of videos
evaluations.rationale: “Segmentation” is ambiguous (shots, scenes, chapters, arbitrary segments) and “validate” criteria are unclear.

evaluations.evidence: annotate news video segments and extract a topic for each segment
evaluations.rationale: “Topic” is ambiguous (taxonomy label, free text, multiple topics) and “extract” could be manual vs automated.

evaluations.evidence: filter and rank videos based on A/V quality aspects
evaluations.rationale: “A/V quality aspects” is vague (resolution, bitrate, loudness, artifacts, etc.), enabling different ranking rules.

evaluations.evidence: quick assessment of whether audio material has been edited before the upload
evaluations.rationale: “Quick assessment” and what counts as “edited” (cut, normalized, compressed, filtered) are ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: prefilter nudity content
evaluations.rationale: “Nudity content” and “prefilter” thresholds/actions (block, flag, blur) are unclear and can vary materially.

evaluations.evidence: prefilter content using search based on low­level asset information
evaluations.rationale: “Low-level asset information” is an abstraction with multiple interpretations (technical metadata, features, hashes).

evaluations.evidence: automatically validated the ingested contents for copyright infringement
evaluations.rationale: “Validated” and what constitutes “copyright infringement” detection (matching, policy thresholds, jurisdictions) are ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: high­level asset information such as metadata and tags either recognized by the system of provided by the user
evaluations.rationale: “High-level asset information” and “recognized by the system” are vague; scope of metadata/tags and recognition method unclear.

evaluations.evidence: assess how interesting or appealing or complex a picture is
evaluations.rationale: “Interesting,” “appealing,” and “complex” are subjective and allow materially different interpretations/metrics.

evaluations.evidence: detect when a scientist should be prompted to look at a subject
evaluations.rationale: “Should be prompted” and criteria for prompting are unclear; “subject” meaning is also not defined here.

evaluations.evidence: identify volunteer types
evaluations.rationale: “Volunteer types” is undefined (skill level, behavior clusters, demographics), leading to different categorizations.

evaluations.evidence: preclassify the Galaxy Zoo images using simple low­level image features
evaluations.rationale: “Preclassify” and “simple low-level image features” are vague; classification targets and feature set are unclear.

evaluations.evidence: detect Snapshot Serengeti images with no classifiable animals in them
evaluations.rationale: The intent is clear: identify images lacking animals that can be classified; while thresholds may vary, the requirement has a single main interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: automatic image series detection for the case of timestamping malfunction
evaluations.rationale: “Image series detection” and what constitutes “timestamping malfunction” are underspecified, enabling different detection behaviors.

evaluations.evidence: automatic animal species preclassification in Snapshot Serengeti
evaluations.rationale: “Preclassification” is ambiguous (coarse vs fine species, confidence thresholds, output format).

evaluations.evidence: automatic animal attribute preclassification
evaluations.rationale: “Attribute” is undefined (age, sex, behavior, pose, etc.), allowing materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: automatic animal number detection
evaluations.rationale: “Number detection” could mean count individuals, estimate range, or detect presence of multiple; counting rules are unclear.

evaluations.evidence: automatic segmentation or localization of plankton
evaluations.rationale: “Segmentation” vs “localization” are different outputs; using “or” leaves materially different interpretations of what is required.

evaluations.evidence: detect Plankton Portal images with no classifiable plankton in them
evaluations.rationale: Single clear intent: find images without plankton that can be classified; not materially open to multiple meanings.

evaluations.evidence: detection of plankton size or orientation
evaluations.rationale: “Size” (area, length, diameter, units) and “orientation” (angle definition) are underspecified; “or” also leaves scope ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: preclassification of plankton species
evaluations.rationale: “Preclassification” lacks clarity on taxonomy level, confidence thresholds, and output, allowing different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: worm motion analysis to reduce video duration
evaluations.rationale: “Reduce video duration” is ambiguous (speed-up, trim inactive parts, summarize) and “motion analysis” scope is unclear.

evaluations.evidence: detect the time ... where the worm lays an egg
evaluations.rationale: Clear requirement to identify the timestamp/event of egg-laying in the video; minimal room for materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: detect important features such as areas of flooding, damage, temporary shelters, blocked roads etc
evaluations.rationale: “Important features” is vague and “etc” leaves scope open-ended, enabling materially different feature sets.

evaluations.evidence: assess the probability/weight of a volunteer’s classification based on their experience
evaluations.rationale: “Probability/weight” and “experience” are ambiguous (how measured, what model), leading to different scoring requirements.

evaluations.evidence: remove artefacts such as bright stars and camera read errors
evaluations.rationale: “Remove artefacts” is ambiguous (mask, delete images, correct pixels) and examples don’t define full scope/behavior.

evaluations.evidence: detect moving and transient objects
evaluations.rationale: “Transient objects” is unclear (cosmic rays, asteroids, variable stars, noise), allowing different detection targets.

evaluations.evidence: remove background noise and distracting sounds
evaluations.rationale: “Background noise” and especially “distracting sounds” are subjective/vague, leading to different filtering requirements.

evaluations.evidence: group whale calls that are similar
evaluations.rationale: “Similar” is ambiguous (frequency pattern, duration, species, call type), enabling materially different grouping criteria.

evaluations.evidence: identify the number of whales heard in a single audio file
evaluations.rationale: “Number of whales heard” is ambiguous (distinct individuals vs simultaneous callers vs estimated count) and can be interpreted differently.

evaluations.evidence: know when I should interrupt a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: “Interrupt” and criteria for “when” are undefined (timing, triggers, channels), allowing different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: interrupt a volunteer with text, an image, or a video
evaluations.rationale: Still ambiguous on what constitutes an “interrupt” and the decision logic for choosing text/image/video.

evaluations.evidence: know when I should educate a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: “Educate” and the conditions for “when” are vague, leading to different triggering rules and content scope.

evaluations.evidence: educate a volunteer with text, an image, or a video
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous decision criteria for selecting medium and what “educate” entails (tips, tutorial, corrective feedback).

evaluations.evidence: which piece of education I should give to a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: “Piece of education” is unclear (lesson, hint, article, microcopy) and selection criteria are unspecified.

evaluations.evidence: interesting comment on a subject
evaluations.rationale: “Interesting” is subjective and “subject” is not defined here, allowing different detection/trigger interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: when Zoonibot should comment on a subject
evaluations.rationale: “Should comment” criteria and what counts as a “subject” are unclear, enabling different behaviors.

evaluations.evidence: when Zoonibot should give an explanation
evaluations.rationale: “Explanation” and triggering conditions are underspecified, allowing materially different implementations.

evaluations.evidence: what Zoonibot should say to a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: Scope is extremely open-ended; “should say” could mean templates, full NLG, tone rules, or specific messages.

evaluations.evidence: group subjects by similarity
evaluations.rationale: “Subjects” and “similarity” are undefined (visual, metadata, annotation patterns), leading to different grouping requirements.

evaluations.evidence: recommend different projects to volunteers based on their previous experiences
evaluations.rationale: “Previous experiences” is ambiguous (projects joined, classifications, time spent, performance), enabling different recommendation logic.

evaluations.evidence: see a summary of articles, so that I reuse them
evaluations.rationale: “Summary” (length, fields, abstraction level) and “reuse them” are unclear (republish, reference, template), allowing different interpretations.
